agent_priors_used: General prior, not SPIDER evidence: locally rational continuation is a documented failure mode; a lane left on its own next_question drifts toward incremental refinements of a spent thread.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: if comparators sit at ceiling, no treatment effect is identifiable regardless of sample size, so a non-degeneracy/dynamic-range check must precede any benchmark spend.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: end-to-end agent cost is dominated by exploration, verification and repair rather than by stored-representation size, which favors counter-based work-avoided metrics.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: memory/cache invalidation is harder than population and un-questioned stale knowledge is a correctness hazard, so false-accept-first freshness/repair metrics matter more than coverage.
General prior, not SPIDER evidence: a prerequisite observed failing identically across lanes should be repaired once, not rediscovered per lane - but only if it is reachable by an authorized writer.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: serial gating chains make off-path breadth cheap but not free; off-path lanes should be parked or pointed at the highest-value non-gated question rather than kept busy.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: LEGACY: DISTINCT_EXTENSION. The pre-2.0 archive contains bounded graph repair-round artifacts (codex/legacy_artifact_index.json paths results/graph/cycle3_REPAIR_ROUND1_recount.json sha f2239dd8dfb2f4744895bb9c3a6495646cfab31c and results/graph/fused_REPAIR_ROUND1_recount.json sha c7a052ea28929a9a62813b230480118d209eccde; reports/graph/robustness_repair_round1.md sha 032c11f915eb4b235f2cba0fd907f9a81a0122b7) and procedure-compilation reports (reports/graph/procedure_compilation_p0.md sha 12eac599c2e907e442f74d48625bf404b259a74f), but none measures distributed repair cost and contamination bounds under controlled local perturbations against a cold-re-derivation comparator. R2's only strong positive on this claim is the bounded single-node line (EXP-GRAPH-36018188168), which does not establish a reusable multi-node repair capability. This is not a pointless rerun: it changes the measured object away from the parked D1V freshness constructibility read to the starved repair-cost/contamination question, and it explicitly excludes the near-identical state-feature tests the legacy guard forbids.

allocation.question: Can local delta repair, measured on a controlled credential-free multi-node substrate with an independently verifiable local-perturbation surface, repair the inherited knowledge affected by a bounded local change (blast radius 1-3: a changed field, endpoint, transport validator/token, or permission) at repair cost materially below an honest cold re-derivation under identical per-trajectory counters (http_requests + retrieval_calls + verification_calls + repair_attempts), while keeping contamination (incorrectly repaired or falsely accepted items) below a preregistered bound and reporting per-family precision/recall and false-accept, so that C-DELTA-REPAIR's registry next gate (controlled local perturbations with repair cost and contamination bounds) is actually measured rather than re-assumed?
allocation.rationale: Graph is tunnel-flagged (C-FRESHNESS streak 6, 7/10 recent) and its active pre-freeze mandate is a fourth attempt to construct a >=2-anchor D1V population, even though the preceding accepted packet (EXP-GRAPH-37992949248) already reports a single-anchor, transport-coupled population that is time-stable across two capture dates and explicitly PARKS the four-anchor Part II route. Spending another cycle confirming a precondition the Codex already indicates is unreachable has low marginal value. Meanwhile C-DELTA-REPAIR is the most neglected priority claim (1 recent-window packet; last finalized packet EXP-GRAPH-36106653880 was MEASUREMENT_INVALID; no active mandate) and repair is the loop's terminating safety action, so a repair-cost/contamination result is both scientifically live and directly product-relevant. A cognitive reset on today's Codex selects the neglected, product-central, still-unmeasured repair question over the spent freshness constructibility probe.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: Effective claim state is unchanged from the last sync and all six lanes are live with active PREFREEZE experiments; no frozen experiment is awaiting completion. The program's one decisive deliverable is still an external-agent demonstration that inherited procedures/mechanisms cut fully loaded cost per successful task, and that deliverable is serially gated by the three blockers the prior cycle identified correctly: B1 (shipped audited parameterized carrier plus a known-negative refusal), B2 (a task bank whose cold/retrieval comparators are genuinely below ceiling), B3 (a same-model endpoint that can actually perform the minimal multi-step Web task). I therefore keep Product, Runtime and Intel dedicated to B1/B2/B3 and refuse to fund any full four-arm C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON execution this cycle (readiness conditions 1-3 are all still missing). The off-path lanes are re-pointed instead of left to local inertia: Graph is pivoted off its own already-parked, structurally degenerate C-FRESHNESS four-anchor route to the starved priority claim C-DELTA-REPAIR; Frontier is pivoted off a C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE micro-benchmark that has now lost three consecutive packets to a shared control-plane defect, onto the genuinely architecture-changing acquisition-cost question; Physics keeps its orthogonal, product-relevant endpoint-barrier-stationarity question with an attainability certificate. Portfolio yield remains the dominant non-scientific cost (255/434 REVISE+MEASUREMENT_INVALID) and the same-failure counters (Product 11, Intel 11, Frontier 9) confirm that repeated control-plane design defects, not lack of activity, are the bottleneck. The freeze-time code-binding defect is real but lives in scripts/, outside every lane's allowed_code_roots, so no lane is assigned to 'repair' it; mandates are instead written to avoid re-requiring the unsatisfiable V9 literal.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The Scout is not degraded (model_scout status=success), so its brief is staff advice cross-checked against the Codex claim state, not authority. It materially shaped this cycle in three ways. (1) I accept its central read that B1/B2/B3 form a serial gate and that Product/Runtime/Intel are each already pointed at one blocker, so all three stay CONTINUE/USE rather than being re-rotated. (2) I accept its challenge to Frontier's C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE pivot and pivot Frontier to the acquisition-cost / site-native-discovery question; I reject its alternative orthogonal probes because structured intent canonicalization duplicates C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE, incremental/delta propagation duplicates the C-DELTA-REPAIR work I am assigning to Graph, and compile-then-replay is close to SPIDER's own core and to the withdrawn 8.5x replay claim. (3) I partially reject its suggestion that Graph should merely honor its fail-loudly clause: the preceding accepted packet already parked the four-anchor Part II route, so I supersede the constructibility probe outright and redirect Graph to the starved C-DELTA-REPAIR claim. I also answer its open question about the shared freeze-time code-binding defect by NOT assigning any lane to repair it (scripts/ is outside every lane's allowed code roots) and by writing mandates that avoid the unsatisfiable V9 literal. Its external notes on budget-matched memory negatives, stale-memory benchmarks and strong browser-agent baselines are recorded as design priors for the eventual flagship benchmark, not as SPIDER evidence.
